To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the accuracy metric that best fits the user utility function is the one that uses the utility function and a sigmoid functional decision threshold, (2) a user-specific decision threshold is more appropriate than a pointwise decision threshold, and (3) the accuracy metrics that are most suitable for a user can be determined by using a user model that is trained on data from that same user.

(i) the proposed user-specific accuracy metrics are more accurate than state-of-the-art metrics, (ii) the proposed metrics are not only better for users with extreme preferences, but also for users with moderate preferences, (iii) the proposed metrics can be used for any type of recommender system, and (iv) the proposed metrics have a high potential to improve the effectiveness of recommenders.

(1) the accuracy metrics that take the user-specific pointwise decision threshold into account outperform the state-of-the-art accuracy metrics that do not; (2) the accuracy metrics based on the user-specific utility function and sigmoid decision threshold further improve on the accuracy metrics that rely solely on the pointwise decision threshold; (3) the user-specific accuracy metrics are not only more user-specific than the state-of-theart accuracy metrics, but also more user-specific than each other.
